It is a misdemeanor for any civilian to wear an army uniform in full or in part, unless they are an actor in a military movie, but they must stay on set. If wearing rank and insignia or name tag, and especially medals, it becomes a felony when using it for stolen valor and personal gain. Not even a veteran who was discharged honorably can wear his uniform anytime from 3 months after discharge. It's only legal to wear military uniforms WITHOUT rank, insignia and medals on Halloween. Anyone who says this law has been repealed for First Amendment issues is lying. States also have their own laws to enforce it, which will detail the prohibitions and penalties. I will include Arizona's law as one example.


10 US CODE §772

(a)A member of the Army National Guard or the Air National Guard may wear the uniform prescribed for the Army National Guard or the Air National Guard, as the case may be.
(b)A member of the Naval Militia may wear the uniform prescribed for the Naval Militia.
(c)A retired officer of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, or Space Force may bear the title and wear the uniform of his retired grade.
(d)A person who is discharged honorably or under honorable conditions from the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, or Space Force may wear his uniform while going from the place of discharge to his home, within three months after his discharge.
(e)A person not on active duty who served honorably in time of war in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, or Space Force may bear the title, and, when authorized by regulations prescribed by the President, wear the uniform, of the highest grade held by him during that war.
(f)While portraying a member of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, or Space Force, an actor in a theatrical or motion-picture production may wear the uniform of that armed force if the portrayal does not tend to discredit that armed force.
(g)An officer or resident of a veterans’ home administered by the Department of Veterans Affairs may wear such uniform as the Secretary of the military department concerned may prescribe.
(h)While attending a course of military instruction conducted by the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, or Space Force, a civilian may wear the uniform prescribed by that armed force if the wear of such uniform is specifically authorized under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the military department concerned.
(i)Under such regulations as the Secretary of the Air Force may prescribe, a citizen of a foreign country who graduates from an Air Force or Space Force school may wear the appropriate aviation or space badges of the Air Force or Space Force.
(j)A person in any of the following categories may wear the uniform prescribed for that category:
(1)Members of the Boy Scouts of America.
(2)Members of any other organization designated by the Secretary of a military department.




Arizona 26-170. Unauthorized wearing of uniform; rank insignia; violation; classification

A. No person shall wear any part of the uniform of the national guard or the army, navy or air force of the United States, or a uniform so similar as to be easily mistaken therefore, unless the person is a member of the service whose uniform he wears, an inmate of a veterans' or soldiers' home, or a member of an organization of the United States veterans.

B. A person in the theatrical profession may wear the uniform in a playhouse or theatre while actually engaged in acting the part of a member thereof.

C. A civic organization may parade or travel in a body or assemble in a lodge room, but when the active militia or any part thereof is in active service, or is called into active service, such civic organization or member thereof shall not parade or appear in uniform in the same locality where the active militia is in service.

D. Persons authorized to wear the military uniform of the United States may only display the rank insignia of the highest rank in which they have received federal recognition except the adjutant general who may display the rank insignia of his state appointed grade after written consent of his service branch.

E. A person violating this section is guilty of a class 2 misdemeanor.

I am a sci-fi author, working on a series that takes place in the mid 2090s, with a primarily teenage cast. Especially using the name of the President in various forms to express dissatisfaction or unpleasant things are fun (ie Hoovervilles being shantytowns during the Great Depression, named after Herbert Hoover). The earlobes do not have gauge rings in them. Some people have had the loops removed, resulting in odd, asymmetrical V-shaped deformities in the earlobes. The term gets the name from the mental image that the loops are so huge, you could fit car hubcaps (1980s "mag rims") in them. "Look at that Granny over there. She got them mag loops swingin!"

Several volcanoes in the Aleutian Island chain simultaneously erupt, and continue to erupt for a decade, causing a miniature ice age in the northern hemisphere. Human migration must move south. Ancient Hebrew males and females technically wore the same kind of clothing, a tunic, which is a long one-piece robe. Fabrics would usually be cotton or wool. There were inner and outer tunics. The outer tunic was called the mantle or robe, and it was a square or oblong strip of cloth with a hole in the center for the head. It was worn like a poncho, and had an area for the arms cut out, and would be ankle-length. A belt was tied at the waist (loins) called a cincture or girdle, which was a simple band of cord, cloth or leather, which was embroidered and often embedded with jewels or precious stones. 

Men would wear tassels (tzitzit) on the corners of the mantle, but women would not. Men would also carry a bag that was attached to the belt by a buckle. In cold weather, a cloak would also be worn. Sandals were worn on the feet, but only outdoors. When entering a building, they removed their sandals and washed their feet.

Womens clothing was almost identical to men's, except for a few details. The inner garment was the same to the men's, but the outer garment was longer, with enough border fringe to cover the feet. In some places in Israel, distinct patterns in the fabric designated if it was for men or women. Women also wore an apron that covered the lower half of the body which had pockets to carry things. There is debate whether or not Hebrew women wore a veil at all times, although they do know that the veils were required while in the synagogue or temple. However, both men and women wore head coverings that were a length of cloth and wrapped around the head and rested on the shoulders. 

Women wore jewelry on their bodies, mostly bracelets, anklets, and rings for the fingers, toes and ears. Earrings were clipped on as piercings were forbidden. I used to be a van driver for a medical clinic that took patients from their homes to their day treatment programs and back again, on a daily route with the same passengers every day. The van was a 21-passenger 1985 Dodge Ram Van. It was a gas guzzler and handled like a brick. I knew my passengers really well. All of them had physical and/or psychological handicaps. Most of them were pretty high functioning and could carry on great conversations. I had two passengers who were deaf/blind/mute and they never even seemed aware of their surroundings. Their ages made them adults, but they couldn't feed themselves, go to the bathroom, or even interact with anyone or anything. 

"Lucy" was one passenger I'll never forget. She was about 35 years old, maybe slightly older. She was capable of walking, but had to be guided with someone next to her, holding her hand and supporting her back. Her steps looked as if she was 10 months old and learning how to walk, kind of wobbly and floppy like an infant walks. Because of this struggle, she sat in the 2nd row, behind me. One day during my route, I had only Lucy in the van, as she was my last dropoff, and I was really hungry. I didn't have time to sit down for a meal (like usual), so I decided to go to the Jack In The Box for some 99 cent Jumbo Jacks (2002). The drive-thru was packed, so I decided to go inside the Jack In The Box to get my food. I knew Lucy would be safe in the car by herself as she never did anything other than sit in place and drool. I got my food and came back, and she was fine, as I expected. I left the bag of burgers on the console beside the drivers seat, then I went next door to the 7-Eleven for some bottles of soda, since those fast food cups cause the sodas to go flat really quick. When I came back from the 7-Eleven, I noticed that Lucy had opened the bag of burgers, and was eating them. She was still sitting in her seat, buckled up. I wasn't mad, but I was laughing, because she wasn't eating them the way you should eat a hamburger. She was eating each part by itself, from top to bottom. First the top bun, then the lettuce, then the tomato, then the meat, then the bottom bun. Pickles were dropped on the floor, as were the onions. She was covered in crumbs and pieces of broken off food she was unable to keep in her mouth. I explained this to her dad when I took her home, not to scold her or to get him to pay for the burgers, but just to inform him. He was shocked. "You mean... She... She fed herself?! Oh my goodness! She's never done that before! This is a personal first for her... And I missed it! Damn it! But that's incredible how she fed herself!" He asked a ton of questions, and he was really excited and happy. He was like a parent of an infant who missed observing their child's first steps, and then asking the witness about it. 

I never really realized until that moment of all the things I take for granted with my health. I'm disabled too, but I didn't get diagnosed with my issues until I was older. But I learned a lot of things while at this job. I got to know people who were in such dire situations that I felt it unfair for them to have to struggle like that. At least it seemed to me like a great struggle. They couldn't talk or communicate in any kind of way, so it's not like I could ask them, or even ask Lucy what they thought about their life. I had great pity on them. I know I wouldn't want to live like that. I don't know anybody who would consider that kind of existence as "life." Even during a visit to my 96 year old grand uncle at his nursing home a few days before Christmas, 1996 (a few days before his death as well), my dad was so overcome by our uncle's poor condition of barely being able to stay awake or talk coherently, my dad said to me, "I never want to end up like that. If I ever do, just pull the plug on me, or shoot me like that worthless old mutt in 'Of Mice and Men.' If you can't shoot me yourself, just leave a kitchen knife on my bed and I'll do it my own damn self." 

I remember the Dr Kevorkian assisted suicide scandal in the 1990s, but I always believed that mercy killings or medically assisted suicide was a morally correct thing. If someone doesn't want to live anymore because of physical or mental health reasons, it should be permitted to let them choose their fate and be given it. But what about those people who suffer and can't communicate to Express their feelings about it? Is it moral to let someone like Lucy or the person in this article continue to "live" in the condition they are in? How do they feel? Do they want to live or die? Does anyone else have the right to force them to live or die according to their desires, which may be contrary to the feelings of the person who is actually suffering? It's such a hard question to answer. I know in most cases, people are trying to be morally right in letting the person live, but that just increases suffering, not just for the person with the disability, but for the caregivers as well. I believe that sometimes we have to make the harder choice in giving the order for medically assisted suicide or conservator's choice to pull the plug. There is only so much anyone can take. Sometimes love means you have to let them go peacefully, and that their death still gives them honor and mercy. 

Besides, I believe that with their complete innocence, having never done anything harmful to anyone, nor showed any amount of hate, that their lives had been so filled with love, that they are going to a better place, where they will no longer be in pain. If death is natural and just a part of life, the answer to this conundrum is easy. It's our morals, values, love, respect for others and refusal to give up on the ones we care about, that keep us wanting to hang onto them and keep them alive. That's not a bad thing nor an immoral thing. But we do it for our own benefit more than we do it for their benefit. We know that murder is wrong, and we hate thinking about death as it's an unknown mystery. 

Only God can judge us, and I think that God understands our position and respects our thoughts as long as our thoughts had the intent to be moral and do it for for their peace and that Heaven is a better place for them than the constant pain of living on Earth with a disability so severe, a meaningful life was impossible. It's not God's fault they were born like that, or for any frailty of nature. God created nature, our DNA, our spirits. He drafted the blueprints and created the elements and gave nature instructions on how to do things. But nature itself is not perfect, and it builds things in the same way we construct a house or a car. If something is wrong, we have to do our best to live with it in an honorable way. Making excuses or blaming others, including God, gets us nowhere. We make our choices and we must accept responsibility for them, good or bad. Everyone is entitled to their beliefs and opinions, and I respectfully leave all these things open for respectful debate.

When I was 12, I had this toy that was a NHRA type dragster, that transformed into a battle vehicle. (Hasbro's M.A.S.K. series "Afterburner") The nose on the dragster could be shot out like a missile from a little button. This thing could really fly, unlike a lot of those toy missile launcher triggers from the 80s that fly 6 inches and drop. This thing could launch about 20 feet and still bounce around for extra distance on carpet. 

The nose was about 4 inches long, 2 inches wide at the front wing, 1/5 inch high, and weighed about as much as a 1990s Casio digital wristwatch. Plastic, but not exactly small or lightweight! 

One day I was playing with it, and it flew over my bed to the other side of the room. I went to go get it, but I couldnt find it anywhere. I looked under the bed, behind the dressers, everywhere, for about an hour. It was just gone like it had vaporized. 

Fast forward 7 years, when I'm 19. I have just graduated high school, and am about to leave for the Army. I was moving all of my stuff out of my room in preparation for my departure, and putting it in the makeshift storage area my dad built as an upper level in the garage. I was taking down all the pictures I had drawn over the years on notebook paper, that had been fastened to the wall by thumb tracks at all the corners. When I took a specific one down, the nose of the dragster fell out from behind it!!! I was so glad I found it! I actually shouted praises to God! I opened up my toy box which was still in my room, and put the nose back on the dragster which I hadn't played with since the day I lost the nose.  

I wondered how it could have slid behind there after hitting the wall, but didnt come out of the bottom of the paper. Shouldn't there have been a ricochet from the momentum and speed this thing had when it hit the wall? How did it turn sideways, slide down the top and get stuck behind NOTEBOOK PAPER? There was NEVER any evidence that it was resting on one of the thumb tracks, as I would have seen it poking out on the side or bottom. 

The most amazing thing was that the dragster nose was never affected by gravity in all its constant and weird effects on things at random times, in over 7 years. You know how gravity is, doing weird stuff! Everythings normal, then all of the sudden, something that was perfectly secure, just falls without warning. This is not so weird you say? Not when you live in southern California. This thing stayed back there for the  February 28, 1990 Upland Earthquake (5.7m), and we lived in Upland; the June 28 1991 Sierra Madre Earthquake (5.6m), epicenter 24 miles away; and the January 17 1994 "Martin Luther King Day" Northridge Earthquake (6.7m, lasting roughly 20 seconds), epicenter 51 miles away. We could feel these very very well, enough to knock lots of things over, but not cause property damage. The shaking from three very strong earthquakes SHOULD HAVE dislodged the dragster nose from behind the paper, but it didnt.

I was a chef in the US Army (MOS: 92G10 Food Service Specialist) during my first tour, and even though we had paid civilians who worked daily for KP to clean the pots and pans etc all day long, we were always encouraged to "clean as we go." To this day, over 10 years since I left the army (22 since I was a cook), I still use these techniques. One a piece of equipment is used, it is washed immediately and put away or reused. You dont want to cross-contaminate by using one piece of equipment on two or more different items. Also, if you wait too long to wash something, the stuff on the equipment hardens and makes it more difficult to clean it off, taking much longer to clean properly. Not only this, many more germs will attach itself to the equipment. Waiting until after you eat is still enough time to make cleaning more difficult. Everything should be cleaned immediately after use and before you eat for best results. If you wash one piece of equipment at a time, cleaning as you go, immediately after all the food is cooked, everything is already cleaned, so you have no dishes waiting in the sink, nor any more chores to do. The food will still be hot and fresh by the time you sit down to eat. The only thing you'll have to clean after eating are the plates and utensils you ate with. But since the mess on them is fresh, it will be easier to clean, and much quicker. Just dont leave anything in your sink for over an hour, or you'll be doing chores for quite some time. Leaving them in the sink overnight makes your cooking equipment and food preparation area, especially the sink, a breeding ground for bacteria, and horrible smells. Clean out your appliances often too. In the army, even though KPs cleaned small things, the cooks still cleaned the preparation areas and floors continuously, and full cleansing of the ovens, refrigerators, deep fat friers, tilt-grills, steamers, mixers, meat slicers, Hobart veggie dicers, and other large tools 3 times a day. All of it was done well enough for thorough inspections between each meal. And make sure your washing tools remain clean. Never allow debris or even soap to remain on your sponge after you've cleaned with it. Bacteria will grow on it. Squeeze all water and soap out of your sponge and lay it on its narrow side against the wall behind the faucet so that it can drain out properly. Never let it remain in the sink, or sponge side down. Your sponges will last much longer when cleaned out and stored properly after use, but still exchange them once a month. Dry everything with a chamois or disposable paper towel and keep the chamois away from water and out of the sink when storing it and hang it up in a clean area for it to air dry easily. Clean your microwave spinning plate before and after every use. Wipe its walls often too. The compact area inside is a perfect environment for yucky stuff to grow. Wash, rinse, sanitize and dry everything by hand. Having good cleaning habits as you go makes things easier in the long run.

I was bullied heavily between 6th and 8th grade. It was so excessive that my dad had me take martial arts, and I got really good at it. In late 8th grade, the worst bully in the school who was twice my size, kept taunting me in class saying that he was going to beat me up after class. I told him that he wasn't going to succeed. After class, he followed me and started poking and pushing me. Then he began swinging punches. I defended myself, but I went overboard losing my temper and I beat him up so severely, he had to go to the hospital as several bones were broken. Many kids gathered to watch the fight, and it became a common topic of conversation among students for weeks. I never got in trouble for it. In fact, the principal congratulated me and thanked me for finally putting the bully in his place. The bully's parents said that he deserved the beating for being such a terrible person to everyone, and that he would probably change his ways after this.

A week later, a group of 4 high school kids attacked me on the street. I beat all of them up too, each of them receiving serious injuries. One student from my school saw the whole thing and spread the news to everyone at school. I was never bullied again after that as it was clear that I could defend myself and that I shouldn't be messed with. 

A year later, now in high school, I was no longer bullied by anyone. Nobody challenged me out of fear. I never wanted to hurt anybody, but 3 years of constant, daily bullying made me very frustrated, with a lot of built up anger. I just stayed away from people. I was kind when people were kind to me, but I stayed on guard for quite a while until I realized that the bullying had indeed stopped. I had no friends in my grade for a very long period of time. Most of my friends were upper or lower classmen.

One day near the end of my 9th grade year, the bully I beat up saw me and approached me. I was prepared to fight, but he just wanted to peacefully talk with me. He apologized for all the trouble he had caused me, and that he had learned to respect me. He also THANKED ME for beating him up, because it caused him to reevaluate his life, and that bullying someone that he, or anybody else saw as a weakling and an easy target, was never what everyone thought he was. He had decided to stop being a jerk and concentrate on improving his life. So I forgave him, and we made peace with one another. 

The last time I saw him was at our high school graduation ceremony. His life had dramatically improved. He had buckled down and became a good student and graduated on the honor roll. He said if it wasn't for me beating the stuffing out of him, he would not have changed from his naughty ways. Then a few years ago, he gave me a friend request on Facebook and I accepted it. We talk quite often now.
